title: Module 9 intro — Production Monitoring and Reliability

lines: Welcome to Module Nine: Production Monitoring and Reliability.
Your model is deployed; now it has to keep working for real users, every day.
Picture a phone company's support bot, the morning after a big marketing campaign.
Traffic triples, and customers say the bot feels slow.
The dashboard shows TTFT jumping from under half a second to three seconds.
Yet time per output token is flat, and errors haven't moved.

say.0: The dashboard shows time to first token jumping from under half a second to three seconds.

lines: That pattern points at the queue: requests wait before prefill even starts.
Queue depth had been climbing for twenty minutes, with no alert.

say.0: That pattern points at the queue: requests wait before pre-fill even starts.

lines: They scale out, and two weeks later a quieter problem appears.
Every dashboard is green, yet customer satisfaction keeps falling.
A new plan has launched, and users ask questions the bot has never seen.
GPU metrics can't see wrong answers; drift and quality checks can.

say.1: G P U metrics can't see wrong answers; drift and quality checks can.

lines: This module teaches you to catch both kinds of failure early.
Lesson one starts with the golden signals of LLM serving.

say.1: Lesson one starts with the golden signals of L L M serving.

lines: You'll track TTFT, time per token, queue depth, KV-cache use and errors.
Always as percentiles, because averages hide the slow tail.

say.0: You'll track time to first token, time per token, queue depth, K V cache use and errors.

lines: Prometheus scrapes vLLM, Triton, NIM and the DCGM exporter, and Grafana draws the dashboards.
Alert on symptoms users feel, then diagnose with causes like GPU Xid errors.

say.0: Prometheus scrapes V L L M, Triton, nim and the D C G M exporter, and Grafana draws the dashboards.
say.1: Alert on symptoms users feel, then diagnose with causes like G P U zid errors.

lines: Logs and traces show which request failed, and where.
OpenTelemetry follows it through retriever and model, and PII is redacted before anything is stored.

say.1: Open Telemetry follows it through retriever and model, and P I I is redacted before anything is stored.

lines: Then you'll detect drift in prompt length, topics and embeddings.
An LLM judge scores a small sample of live answers, to catch silent quality drops.

say.1: An L L M judge scores a small sample of live answers, to catch silent quality drops.

lines: Lesson two covers the model lifecycle.
A version bundles weights, tokenizer, chat template, prompts and generation settings in a registry.
Every candidate must pass the same regression suite as production.
Then it rolls out gradually: shadow traffic first, then a small canary.
If the canary's scores slip, traffic swings back to the previous version, still warm.
Rollback should be fast, rehearsed and boring.
Quality drops, drift and user feedback trigger a reproducible retraining pipeline.
But stale facts are fixed by updating the RAG index, not the weights.

say.1: But stale facts are fixed by updating the rag index, not the weights.

lines: By the end, you'll build LLM dashboards with SLO alerts, catch drift, and ship new versions safely.
Let's begin with lesson one: observability.

say.0: By the end, you'll build L L M dashboards with S L O alerts, catch drift, and ship new versions safely.
